text.p: Following are the main stories in Monday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad reaffirmed that there was no plan for a cabinet reshuffle. The position vacated by Trade and Consumer Affairs Minister Abu Hassan Omar, who moves as chief minister of Selangor state, will be filled, but no other changes will be made, he told reporters at Gaborone in Botswana.

-- Palm oil producer Sikap Group has proposed that the government set up a fund to help local companies setting up ventures abroad affected by policy changes in those countries. Sikap was recently a victim of Indonesia's decision to ban further foreign investment in the oil palm sector.

-- The new Kuala Lumpur International Airport is about 75 percent complete, its chairman Clifford Herbert said. The nine billion ringgit ($3.6 billion) airport would be fully operational in another 135 days.

-- YPJ Gas Sdn Bhd signed an agreement with Petronas Dagangan Bhd to operate gas supplies to 16 housing projects in Kuala Lumpur and its surroundings. YPJ plans to invest five million ringgit to develop a network over the next five years.

-- The new management team led by Maju Holdings Bhd of recently privatised Perwaja Steel Sdn Bhd is increasing productivity, reducing operational costs and shifting focus to special steel products in an effort to revive the ailing national steelmaker.
